transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s my eating. My appetite’s been kind of all over the place for a few months. Some days I just skip dinner and I’ve lost some weight without really trying. Other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels… pointless.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that it’s hard to get interested in activities, even things you used to like?
Yeah… I think so. I still do things, like water the garden or go to book club sometimes, but it doesn’t really… feel like much. I usually leave early, or I just don’t get started in the first place.
Would you say you feel down or depressed most of the day, more days than not?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say most of the day, exactly. I just feel kind of low, I guess. It comes and goes.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
I’m… not really sure. I don’t think I’d say nearly every day. It’s there sometimes, but I don’t know that it’s most of the day.
Can you describe what a typical low mood feels like for you, and how long it usually lasts once it starts?

It’s hard to describe. It’s just kind of… heavy, maybe. Like I’m not really looking forward to anything. Sometimes it passes after a bit, sometimes it hangs around longer. I don’t really track it closely.
When you feel this low mood, do you also notice that you have less energy than usual or feel fatigued, even after resting?
Yeah… I do notice that. Even when work isn’t especially busy, I feel like I’m sort of dragging myself through the hospital. Then when I get home, I’m too tired to cook or really do much.
When you do things you used to enjoy, like your book club or gardening, do you find that you don’t get the same pleasure out of them anymore?
Yeah… I guess so. I still do some of it, like watering the garden or going to book club, but it just feels kind of flat most of the time. Sometimes I leave early, or I just don’t get started at all.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not worth much, even when there’s no real reason for it?
Yeah… sometimes. Mostly I keep going back over the marriage and thinking I must’ve failed at something really basic. I know, logically, it’s more complicated than that, but… it still feels that way.
Can you say for sure if your low mood tends to last throughout most of the day, and if it happens nearly every day, even if it varies a bit in intensity?
I’m not sure I can say for sure. It’s… there a lot, but I don’t really track whether it’s most of the day every day. Some days are worse than others.
Can you tell me if there are days when you don't feel low at all, or does it tend to be present most of the time even if it varies in how strong it is?
I don’t know… I think it’s around more often than not, but I haven’t really noticed if there are whole days where it’s completely gone. It sort of comes and goes in the background.
Can you recall if there have been days in the past two weeks when you didn’t feel low at all, or has it been present in some form every day?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track that closely… I can’t honestly say whether there was a full day where it wasn’t there at all.
Looking back at the last two weeks, would you say that your low mood has been present for most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's not always the same intensity?
I… I still don’t think I can say that clearly. It’s been there off and on, maybe in the background a lot, but I’m not sure about “most of the day” or “nearly every day.”
Let’s focus on the past two weeks. On how many days would you say you felt low for most of the day, rather than just off and on?
I’m not sure I can put a number on it. Maybe a few days? It’s hard to separate “most of the day” from just… on and off.
Can you recall a time when you felt low for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?
I don’t know… I can’t really recall it clearly enough to say. Maybe there have been stretches, but I’m not sure it was most of the day nearly every day for two full weeks.
Can you think back to any specific two-week period in the past few months when you felt low most of the day, nearly every day, without a break?
I can’t really think of a specific stretch like that. I mean… there have been low periods, but “nearly every day without a break” for two weeks—I’m not sure.
Can you think of any two-week period in the past few months when you felt low most of the day, nearly every day, even if it wasn’t completely constant?
I still can’t really pin down a two-week period like that. There were times I felt pretty low, but whether it was most of the day nearly every day… I’m not sure.
Can you think of any two-week period in the past few months when you felt low most of the day, nearly every day, even if it wasn’t completely constant?
I don’t think I can say that, no. I’ve had low days here and there, but I can’t honestly point to two weeks where it was most of the day nearly every day.
Can you tell me if, in the past few months, there has been a period where you felt low most of the day on most days, even if it wasn’t every single day?
Maybe… but I’m not really sure. I’ve had days where I felt low, yes, but I don’t know that I’d call it a clear period where it was most of the day on most days.
Can you think of any period in the past few months that lasted at least two weeks where you felt low for most of the day, even if it wasn’t every single day?
I really can’t say for sure. I’ve had low stretches, but I don’t know that I’d call any of them two full weeks of feeling that way most of the day.

However, the lack of confirmation about the consistency of symptoms across most days and most of the day rules out the more severe or clear-cut codes like F32.9 and F33.9 for now.

This turn suggests that the patient's low mood is not consistently present most of the day, nearly every day, which rules out more severe forms of major depressive disorder (F32.1, F32.2, F32.3) and recurrent depressive disorder (F33.1, F33.2, F33.3). The focus on the past two weeks and the inability to confirm 'most of the day, nearly every day' points toward unspecified depressive disorder (F32.8, F33.8).
